edits.where: FAQ, What is the monitum in a wedding ceremony?
edits.old: It is the statement in [section 46(1)](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ma196185/s46.html) of the Marriage Act 1961 that a celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination says to you, in front of your witnesses, before you marry. <!-- fact_18 -->
edits.new: It is the statement in [section 46(1)](https://classic.austlii.edu.au/au/legis/cth/consol_act/ma196185/s46.html) of the Marriage Act 1961 that a celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination says to you, in front of your witnesses, before you marry. In it, the celebrant states they are duly authorised by law to solemnise marriages, reminds you of the solemn and binding nature of the relationship you are about to enter, and says what marriage is according to law in Australia. The full wording is quoted above. <!-- fact_18 -->
edits.why: Consider (search_visitor): answer did not say what the monitum covers. Summary uses only fact_18 wording (authorised; solemn and binding nature; marriage according to law in Australia).
